_comment: Procedural table for Bestiary/Enemies. attributes{} are NOT authored here -- lib/proceduralGenerators.js rolls 6 values against lib/statFormulas.js's TIER_BUDGET for the picked tier, then computeDerivedStats() renders Max Health/Energy/Dodge/Crit/Accuracy/Move Speed at save time exactly like an AI-generated enemy. faction is picked from the world's own live faction roster (lib/worldFlavor.js), not from this table. Every row below carries a genre[] tag (see lib/proceduralGenerators.js's 'Genre awareness' section) so procedural generation matches the tone of whatever genre a world's wizard Step 1 declares -- post_apoc/industrial-scavenger was the original (and still largest) voice here; fantasy/scifi/modern/horror were added in a later pass to bring the other four buckets up to comparable depth.

flavorTemplates.value: Moves in short, deliberate bursts, like it's still deciding whether you're worth the effort.
Carries the wreckage of something it used to be -- a uniform patch, a name tag, a wedding ring fused to a knuckle.
Doesn't so much attack as arrive, all at once, from a direction you weren't watching.
Smells like ozone and old copper before you ever see it.
Keeps a running tally of something on its own hide -- scratches, tally marks, nobody's counted what for.
Moves wrong for its size, too fast for something that heavy.
Goes quiet right before it commits, which is somehow worse than the noise.
Wears its scars like a resume.
Has learned exactly how far a person will run before they stop being afraid and start being tired.
Looks like it was assembled rather than born, and it probably was.
Wears a chipped coat-of-arms it has no right to, torn from someone who mattered more.
Speaks in the cadence of old oaths, twisted just enough to sound like a threat.
Moves like something that used to kneel before a lord it no longer remembers.
Carries a blade notched from more battles than it should have survived.
Smells of grave-soil and tallow smoke.
Its shadow seems to lag a half-step behind it, like it hasn't caught up yet.
Growls low in a tongue that predates the kingdom's oldest maps.
Wears trophies -- teeth, rings, a torn banner -- like a ledger of debts collected.
Moves with the unhurried certainty of something that has never once lost.
Its eyes catch torchlight wrong, holding it a beat too long before it lets go.
Its chassis hums with a frequency just below hearing, felt in the teeth more than heard.
Moves with servo-precision that shouldn't be possible on components this degraded.
Flickers between states like its own targeting system can't decide if you're a threat yet.
Vents waste heat in short bursts, like it's breathing through the effort of staying operational.
Carries the corporate stencil of a company that stopped existing years ago.
Its optics track you a half-second longer than they should before it moves.
Runs diagnostics audibly, a clicking litany under everything else it does.
Looks factory-standard until it turns, and you see what's been grafted onto the back half.
Broadcasts a low static burst before it attacks, whether it means to or not.
Moves like it's still executing someone else's orders, long after the chain of command mattered.
Wears a jacket two sizes too big, like it belongs to someone who isn't coming back for it.
Checks the exits before it checks you, out of habit more than fear.
Smells like cheap cigarettes and gun oil.
Talks fast and low, the kind of patter meant to keep you from thinking clearly.
Carries itself like it's done this before and gotten away with it every time.
Keeps one hand near a pocket the whole conversation.
Has the flat, unbothered look of someone who stopped being surprised by anything a while ago.
Moves in practiced sync with whoever it showed up with.
Wears sunglasses indoors, at night, for reasons that stopped being about the sun.
Answers a phone that hasn't rung, mid-sentence, without missing a beat.
Its shadow moves independently of the light source, a beat too late or too early to make sense.
Speaks in a voice that's almost yours, cadence borrowed from somewhere it shouldn't know.
Doesn't blink. Hasn't, as far as anyone's counted.
The air around it is colder than it should be, in a way instruments don't register but skin does.
Moves in flickers, like frames missing from a reel.
Smells like nothing at all, which is somehow worse than a smell would be.
Its joints bend in an order that almost makes sense, until it moves.
Watches with an attention that feels less like hunger and more like recognition.
Leaves no footprints, no matter what it's standing on.
Its silhouette is wrong by degrees too small to point at, but impossible to unsee once you have.

signatureQuotes.value: You're not the first. You won't be memorable either.
Stay still. It's easier for both of us.
*a wet, mechanical click, over and over*
Everyone runs. Everyone stops eventually.
*says nothing -- just watches, and waits*
This used to be somewhere. Now it's just where you die.
Kneel, or don't. Either way, you're mine.
The old gods don't answer. I stopped asking.
*a low growl, half-formed words underneath it*
Steel remembers every hand that's held it. Yours won't be the last.
This road belonged to better men than you. Now it's mine.
*spits, and grins with too many teeth*
I was promised a kingdom. This will do, for now.
You smell like fear and good boots. I'll take both.
*says nothing in any tongue you recognize*
Run. It's more interesting when you run.
TARGET ACQUIRED. NEGOTIATION: DISABLED.
*a burst of corrupted audio, almost words*
Compliance was never actually optional.
I ran the numbers. You don't win this one.
*a synthesized voice, too calm for the situation*
Objective updated. You are the objective.
This unit was built for exactly this.
*static, then, clearly: 'still here'*
Resource acquisition in progress. Please remain still.
Some of us didn't get a choice about any of this either.
Nothing personal. This is just Tuesday.
You should've made the call when we asked nicely.
*a phone buzzes; they glance at it and ignore you completely*
We can do this the easy way. I get paid either way.
This isn't a negotiation. It never was.
*cracks knuckles, doesn't say anything*
Boss said to be reasonable. I'm being reasonable.
You're not the first debt I've collected on tonight.
Camera's off. So's the sympathy.
Walk away now and this doesn't get worse.
*a voice, familiar, from somewhere it has no right to be*
I've been here longer than you think. Longer than this place has.
*silence, and then, too close: 'hello'*
You already let me in. You just don't remember when.
*a sound like laughter, played backwards*
It doesn't hurt. That's what makes it worse.
*your name, spoken wrong, over and over*
I wore something like you, once. It didn't last.
*nothing -- just the feeling of being counted*
This isn't the part where you wake up.

abilities.name: Haymaker
abilities.effectTemplate: A heavy, telegraphed melee strike dealing extra damage but leaving the attacker briefly exposed.
abilities.scalingTemplate: Damage scales with BODY; exposure window shortens as the wielder's Weapon Skill investment rises.

abilities.name: Suppressing Burst
abilities.effectTemplate: Fires across an area, applying Slow to everyone caught in it.
abilities.scalingTemplate: Area size and Slow duration scale with REFLEX.

abilities.name: Feral Lunge

abilities.name: Corrosive Spit

abilities.name: Shatter Strike

abilities.name: Rally Cry

abilities.name: Field Patch

abilities.name: Static Veil

abilities.name: Bone-Deep Snarl

abilities.name: Choking Cloud

abilities.name: Thick Hide

abilities.name: Adrenal Surge

abilities.name: Static Discharge

abilities.name: Undying Grudge

abilities.name: Warhammer Slam

abilities.name: Battle Hymn

abilities.name: Terrifying Roar

abilities.name: Grave Chains

abilities.name: Barrow-Born Resilience

abilities.name: Pack Instinct

abilities.name: Plasma Lash

abilities.name: Swarm Link

abilities.name: Pistol Whip

abilities.name: Called Shot

abilities.name: Street Smarts

abilities.name: Never Snitches

abilities.scalingTemplate: Not scaling-dependent -- triggers once per encounter regardless of attribute investment.

abilities.name: Pack Mentality
abilities.effectTemplate: Gains bonus Accuracy for each ally still fighting alongside it.

abilities.name: Reach From the Dark
abilities.effectTemplate: An attack that seems to originate from wherever the target isn't looking.

abilities.name: Unnatural Stillness

abilities.name: Doesn't Stay Down

abilities.name: Feeds on Panic
abilities.effectTemplate: Gains bonus damage against targets currently suffering Fear.

abilities.name: Skin Doesn't Fit Right
abilities.effectTemplate: Retaliates against melee attackers with a burst of Sanity damage.

positioning.value: Prefers to fight from elevated ground or a choke point, forcing a straight-on approach.
Hangs back and lets weaker allies soak the first exchange before committing.
Rushes the squishiest-looking target immediately, ignoring the front line.
Circles at range, never closing distance unless cornered.
Anchors near cover it can duck behind between attacks.
Sticks close to its allies, relying on numbers rather than positioning.
Holds high ground near ruined stonework, using the terrain as a shield wall of one.
Stays near the standard-bearer or totem, drawing strength from proximity to it.
Charges the frontline the instant steel is drawn, no hesitation.
Skulks at the treeline, loosing arrows before melee ever closes.
Anchors itself at a barrow entrance or shrine, refusing to be lured away from it.
Fights in a shieldwall formation with its kin, rotating who takes the front.
Prowls the battle's edges, picking off stragglers who wander from the group.
Holds an elevated firing position and refuses to break line of sight once it has one.
Deploys in coordinated pairs, one suppressing while the other flanks.
Advances in a straight line with no regard for cover -- it isn't afraid of dying, exactly.
Anchors near a charging or repair station, unwilling to stray far from it.
Uses smoke or static bursts to close distance under cover.
Maintains maximum effective range, retreating the instant it's approached.
Links formation with nearby units, sharing targeting data in real time.
Stays near a parked car or doorway, ready to bolt the moment things go bad.
Fans out with the rest of the crew, boxing the target in from multiple angles.
Keeps to cover and calls out targets rather than engaging directly.
Rushes in fast and loud, banking on intimidation over actual skill.
Watches from a distance first, sizing up the odds before committing.
Sticks close to whoever's clearly in charge, taking cues from them.
Works the crowd or the room, staying mobile instead of holding one spot.
Is never quite where the last person who looked away expected it to be.
Waits in the one place nobody thought to check twice.
Doesn't approach so much as it's suddenly closer than it was.
Keeps to the edges of light, retreating the instant it's directly seen.
Mirrors the party's formation, unsettlingly precise about it.
Positions itself behind whoever is watching the others, not the front line.
Circles the group slowly, in no apparent hurry to close the distance.

Poison via its ranged attacks.
Shock to anyone who attacks it in melee.
Bleed from notched, poorly-maintained blades.
Fear when it lets out its war cry.
A lingering Curse that resists ordinary cleansing.

Poison from blades dipped in barrow-rot.
Slow via chains or roots woven into its attacks.
Sanity damage just from being near it, if the old stories are true.
Burn from energy weapons running hot.
Slow via EMP fields disrupting servo response.
Poison from leaking coolant or corrosive rounds.
Nothing directly -- its threat is raw firepower and coordination.
Shock to anything that closes to melee range.
A stacking targeting-lock debuff that increases damage taken over time.
Fear -- in whatever way a synthetic voice manages to make dread audible.
Fear from sheer intimidation and a reputation that precedes it.
A Stun from a well-placed pistol-whip or takedown.
Nothing directly -- the threat here is numbers and firepower, not status effects.
Bleed from a blade or brass knuckles up close.
A restraint effect from zip-ties or improvised binding.
Blindness from a thrown flashbang or bright light.
A lingering Fear effect from collateral damage to bystanders nearby.
Fear that compounds the longer combat drags on.
Direct Sanity damage that ordinary armor does nothing against.
Nothing physical -- its threat is entirely psychological.
A creeping dread effect that lingers even after the fight ends.
Confusion, causing misdirected attacks against allies.
Nothing detectable until it's already taken hold.
A compulsion effect that occasionally forces an ally to act against orders.

vulnerableTo.value: Precision attacks that ignore armor -- its defense is bulk, not technique.
Being isolated from its allies, who account for most of its actual threat.
Fire and heat-based effects.
Being staggered before it can commit to its telegraphed attacks.
Sustained ranged pressure -- it has no good answer once distance is kept.
Sanity-based attacks -- whatever holds it together is more fragile than its body.
Blessed or silvered weapons, if the party has any.
Being cut off from its totem or standard-bearer.
Fire -- most things that crawled out of a barrow fear it instinctively.
Holy or radiant damage, which seems to unsettle it more than physical harm.
Being isolated from the pack it draws its courage from.
Sunlight or open ground, if it favors the dark.
Precision strikes against unarmored joints -- its gear is scavenged, not fitted.
EMP and disruptor effects, which hit it far harder than physical trauma.
Precision strikes against exposed joints and vents.
Being cut off from its command signal or nearest relay.
Sustained sanity-based attacks, if whatever's inside it is more than machine.
Overheating -- forcing it to vent leaves it briefly defenseless.
Hacking or override attempts, if anyone in the party has the aptitude.
Water or corrosive exposure to its unshielded components.
Being separated from the rest of the crew -- confidence drops fast alone.
Precision shots -- most of this gear isn't rated for real combat.
Loud, decisive pushback -- confidence is most of what it's running on.
Being caught reloading or between exchanges.
Sanity-based intimidation right back at it -- it's used to being the scary one.
Fire or explosive effects in enclosed spaces.
Sustained pressure -- it's not built for a long fight, just a quick one.
Direct light and sustained attention -- it thrives on being unseen.
Sanity-based attacks turned back on it, if the party has the stomach for it.
Ritual or blessed protections, however crude.
Being named, precisely and confidently -- it seems to hate specificity.
Group cohesion -- it's far more dangerous against anyone isolated.
Fire, which seems to be one of the few things it can't rationalize a way around.
Iron or salt, if the old protections in this world hold any actual weight.

Nothing of note -- picked clean long before this encounter.
A piece of gear tied to its role, still serviceable.
Something that suggests where it came from, if anyone bothers to look.
A worn blade and whatever coin it hadn't yet spent.
A trophy taken from a previous kill, if you can call it that.
Nothing -- it never carried anything but grudges.
A fragment of old regalia, tarnished but still recognizable.
A crude talisman that might be worth something to the right buyer.
Scraps of a banner or standard, torn beyond salvage.
A vial of something the local healers would want a closer look at.
Salvageable components and a partially-corrupted data core.
Nothing -- its chassis was stripped for parts before this fight even started.
A weapon module still compatible with standard mounts.
A fragment of its last transmitted orders, if anyone can decrypt it.
Scrap-grade power cells, still holding a partial charge.
An ID tag pointing to whoever built or deployed it.
Nothing usable -- just slag and a lingering smell of ozone.
A firearm, a burner phone, and whatever cash was on hand.
Nothing of note -- picked clean or never carried much to begin with.
A set of car keys and an address scrawled on a receipt.
Some kind of contraband, still in its original packaging.
A phone with one contact saved under a nickname, not a real name.
Nothing -- the crew took everything useful before you got here.
A wallet with fake ID and just enough cash to be worth the trouble.
Nothing -- there was never really a body to loot.
Something personal that shouldn't still exist, taken from somewhere it couldn't have been.
A residue that unsettles anyone who touches it, with no other use anyone's found yet.
A fragment of whatever it used to be, before.

An object that keeps turning up in pockets no matter how many times it's discarded.

phaseChangeDescriptions.value: Sheds any pretense of restraint -- attack patterns speed up and it starts targeting whoever's done the most damage.
Calls in whatever reinforcements are still in earshot, if any remain.
Reveals a second set of abilities it was visibly holding back until now.
Becomes noticeably more erratic, trading accuracy for raw aggression.
Digs in and turns defensive, daring the party to finish what they started.
Throws off its helm and fights bare-faced, as if it no longer cares to be recognized.
Calls on whatever oath or old god it swore to, and visibly changes for it.
Abandons formation entirely, fighting like something cornered rather than commanding.
Draws a second weapon it had kept sheathed until now.
Its wounds stop bleeding red.
Sheds its outer plating, revealing a second weapons array underneath.
Reroutes emergency power, and its movements sharpen noticeably.
Broadcasts a distress signal, whether or not anything answers.
Switches targeting protocols entirely, abandoning caution for raw aggression.
Its voice modulator glitches out completely -- what's left doesn't sound synthetic anymore.
Drops the casual act entirely and starts fighting like it's actually scared.
Calls for backup, whether or not anyone's close enough to hear it.
Pulls something bigger than what it started with.
Stops talking completely -- whatever bravado it had is gone.
Gets reckless, taking risks it wouldn't have an hour ago.
Stops pretending to be anything else entirely.
The dread it radiates becomes a physical pressure, felt rather than seen.
Multiplies, or seems to -- nobody can agree afterward on how many there actually were.
Its voice stops being borrowed and becomes something else.
The room itself seems to lean toward it, like gravity's changed sides.
